newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's second city wants to build new airport.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's second city wants to build new airport.

text.p: Ukraine's second largest city Kharkov wants to build a new international airport on the site of its existing military airport, the city council head said on Wednesday.
Yevhen Kushnaryov, quoted by UNIAN news agency, said two foreign companies had shown interest in building a new airport, but did not name the Western firms.
Kushnaryov said that he wanted to hold talks with Ukraine's defence ministry to convert a military airport in the nearby town of Chuhuyev into a civilian complex.
The eastern Ukrainian city, with a population of about two million, has a small Soviet-era civil airport handling 10 international flights a month -- mostly charters and flights to Russia.
Kiev's Borispil airport was renovated a year ago with a loan from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).
The airport in the eastern industrial city of Dnipropetrovsk was also renovated last year but work was sponsored by local businesses.
Germany's Daimler-Benz won a contract last month to renovate the international airport in the Black Sea port of Odessa next year.
